project.name: PracticeTakes
project.description: Practice Takes is an early-stage desktop music-practice application for Windows, Linux, and macOS, built with JUCE 8 and C++20, currently offering a tuner and spectrogram over a shared microphone-capture shell. It also includes a small TypeScript Cloudflare Worker that receives in-app feedback submissions.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: README.md introduces Practice Takes, a JUCE 8 / C++20 desktop music-practice app with a tuner, spectrogram, harmonics and score Target Note tool sharing one capture shell. The architecture document is the map to read before touching ownership, the audio thread or new tools.

tour.title: Entry Point and Shell
tour.description: main.cpp is the JUCE application entry; it owns the top-level window, which owns MainComponent, the application shell. MainComponent coordinates audio state, menus and workspace, and it names no individual tool: it discovers them through the registry.
tour.languageLesson: Pure logic such as WorkspaceLayoutState is kept free of JUCE so it can be unit tested without a display.

tour.title: The Tool Contract
tour.description: Every analysis tool is declared and built through ToolCatalog (JUCE-free identity), ToolRegistry (factories), ToolComponent (what the shell may assume) and ToolServices (the shared-service bundle). ToolComponent is implemented by the four tools, and BuiltInTools.cpp plus BuiltInToolCatalog.h are the single registration site, so adding a tool needs no shell change.

tour.title: Adding a Tool
tour.description: This guide walks through the one-entry-each recipe in the catalog and registration site from the previous step. It also explains the rule that tools reach application state only through ToolServices.

tour.title: Audio Capture and the Real-Time Boundary
tour.description: AudioInputService owns microphone capture and its callback runs on the real-time audio thread, so it must not allocate, lock or log. It only copies samples into preallocated SPSC FIFOs (AudioSampleFifo), one per tool, which tools drain from message-thread timers.
tour.languageLesson: The callback is marked noexcept and PRACTICE_TAKES_NONBLOCKING so a RealtimeSanitizer CI job can catch violations.

tour.title: A Feature Tool: The Tuner
tour.description: The tuner is a ToolComponent that drains its own FIFO from a timer and does pitch analysis on the message thread, which keeps a slow tool from blocking capture. Its settings codec shows how a tool persists state through the shell.

tour.title: MIDI Input and the Score Model
tour.description: MIDI capture mirrors the audio discipline: MidiInputService owns its own MidiInput, and an event FIFO drops the oldest event on overflow. The JUCE-free score model and MusicXML importer feed the Target Note tool through the CurrentScore holder.

tour.title: Score Consumers and Format Rules
tour.description: The Target Note tool is the first consumer of the score model. The musicxml-subset document specifies what the importer accepts, drops or refuses, and the findings document records what consuming the model revealed.

tour.title: Settings and Configuration
tour.description: SettingsPersistence stores settings and defaults, while SettingsTransferCodec handles portable .ptsettings import and export. Transactional import keeps a failed import from corrupting the live settings.

tour.title: Feedback Service
tour.description: In-app feedback goes to a Cloudflare Worker written in TypeScript, backed by SQL migrations, with a Dockerfile for self-hosting. The wire format is documented by a shared JSON schema that nothing yet validates against, so the two sides can drift.
tour.languageLesson: SQL migrations are numbered and applied in order, evolving the schema alongside the code.

tour.title: Tests and the Testing Suite
tour.description: src/tests mirrors src, so each source file has its tests beside the mirrored path, as the audio and tool tests show. A separate Python testing suite runs every suite, records measurements and exports the release-gate record.

tour.title: Build and CI
tour.description: CMake builds the app and test targets, with source lists kept in tools/cmake/Sources.cmake. GitHub Actions workflows cover multiplatform builds, sanitizers and the Pages site.
tour.languageLesson: CMake source lists are plain variables that the root file includes and passes to targets.

tour.title: Docs, OpenSpec and the Knowledge-Graph Site
tour.description: The agent guide and CONTRIBUTING say when a change needs an OpenSpec proposal rather than a plain PR. The Pages workflow publishes the generated architecture map, whose requirements are specified in openspec.
